An English crowd chanting so heartily for a Dutch player is somewhat of a rarity, especially when they are taking on an Englishman, but it was the sensational manner of his victory over the world No 1 and back-to-back Grand Slam champion that won them over. Littler was aiming for a Grand Slam three-peat after his wins in 2024 and 2025 but with the Dutchman prevailing, it is still only Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen who have achieved such a feat. Lewis Hamilton has insisted there is no lack of trust between himself and his Ferrari team despite having overridden orders from the pit wall twice in recent races. At the Singapore Grand Prix in October and the Sao Paulo Grand Prix earlier this month, Hamilton ignored instructions to pit, with his decision costing him places on both occasions. The incidents followed several moments earlier in the season where Hamilton had been left frustrated by strategic decisions from Ferrari that failed to optimise his chances. messages.text: Cadillac confirm Bottas to stay with team for 2027

metadata.summary: Cadillac have confirmed Valtteri Bottas will stay on at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, ending speculation about the Finnish driver's future.
metadata.content: Valtteri Bottas: Cadillac confirm Finnish driver to stay with team for 2027 Formula 1 season ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Valtteri Bottas: Cadillac confirm Finnish driver to stay with team for 2027 Formula 1 season ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix Valtteri Bottas will remain with Cadillac next year after speculation his future at the team was in doubt; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with Friday's practice sessions at 12.30am and 4pm By Nigel Chiu in Las Vegas Wednesday 18 November 2026 20:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking at the Sao Paulo GP, Valtteri Bottas said 'nothing has changed' and he was hopeful of staying with Cadillac for the long term Cadillac have confirmed Valtteri Bottas will stay on at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, ending speculation about the Finnish driver's future. Bottas returned after a year's absence from the grid for this season, Cadillac's first in the sport, as one of two hugely experienced drivers for the all-new American team's first line-up alongside Sergio Perez, who signed a contract extension last month until at least 2029. But, Bottas' future has been up in the air recently as Cadillac pushed for American Formula 2 driver Colton Herta to earn a Formula 1 super licence, which he secured two weeks ago, by running him in practice sessions.
